[Coss](https://s-media-cache-ak0.pinimg.com/736x/ea/32/96/ea3296ab2efc9c4ec810aeefbe8ddee1.jpg) of the [Thorac](https://s-media-cache-ak0.pinimg.com/736x/fa/2f/65/fa2f65f9fbf388f867d3f4b85c8c1acd.jpg) is a legendary warrior. He was blessed with great strength and high endurance. His skill with a spear was unrivaled and he was thought to have been trained by Mars himself. It was clear to the Thorac he *should* have been the one to survive: it was his destiny to defend his people with courage and brawn. Even at a young age, stories were being sung of how he was the hero the prophets had foretold of.

No one hummed a tune for his brother.

In fact, ever since adolescence when the pair grew, it was almost as if he was already dead. He inherited a fraction of the strength and bulk his brother had, and almost seemed to be carried around like a satchel upon Coss's back. Over time, jealousy consumed his body and hate burned through him. He felt overlooked, invisible, and alone for years and years, praying to Dreka to end his miserable and worthless life. When the time came, Coss survived and [Monix](http://www.ancient-origins.net/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/Native-American-long-hair.jpg?itok=frlWPVdm) found peace.

In death, Monix received more recognition than he had for his entire life. Being the sacrifice who allowed the hero to survive, Monix's remains were buried among passed chieftain and priests. His grave marker reminded visitors of his legacy, reading "**that He may live.**" No one bothered to engrave, nor even remember, his name. That is, none except Fec.

Fec smiled upon the Thorac. Not particularly because they worshiped him (they didn't), but because for each Thorac birthing, two corpses would inevitably be buried in the ground. Fec liked corpses. They were left behind by the soul and free to be reanimated. This poor individual, in particular, was especially enticing, as it seemed like the Thorac were *happy* he was dead. They *wanted* Monix to waste away beneath the earth so that they may have their precious hero Coss.

Fec saw an opportunity.

One night, when the moon shone bright above the sleepy horizon, Fec dove down 6 feet in the forgotten's grave and imbued the rotting corpse with his own spirit. Using tooth and nail, Fec dug Monix's cadaver up through the dirt, finally breaching the surface with a [single hand.](http://www.barnesandnoble.com/nook-blog/wp-content/uploads/2013/10/zombie_hand.jpg) Pulling himself free of the unforgiving soil, Fec finally had a chance to examine the corpse he occupied.

"That He may live, indeed" Fec whispered upon catching a glance at the grave marker. "Coss may be the champion of the living, but I will make [Monix the King of the Dead.](http://cdn3.whatculture.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/11/Resident-Evil-Zombie.jpg)"

Fec strode off into the mist with but one thing on his mind: he must plead with Dreka to give him Monix's soul.
